main_text.p: אִסְטְרָטִילּוֹסִין Ch. Capitanei, Duces agminis militaris. A'Graeco στρατηλάτης.
[illegible, ~6 letters] Syr. Luxus, voluptas, deliciae, corruptu ex Graeco τρυφή: [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] Quae servit voluptati, Graec. καταλάω[?], 1. ad Timoth. 5.6.
אִסְטַרְקִילְא Ch. Vox est peregrina & corrupta, Esth. 5.9. Hebraei quidam explicant טם נחשת Laminam aeneam.
אסף [illegible, ~5 letters] Syr. Schola, Gymnasium, σχολή, Act. 19.9. Usitatum est quoque apud Talmudicos.
אִסְכְּלָא Ch. Craticula. Plur. emph. אִסְכְּלָתָא Numer. 31.23. in Jonath.

[illegible, ~6 letters] Syr. Species, Figura, Forma, Habitus. Graec. σχῆμα. Hinc Ch. אִסְכְּמָא רַאיְתָא Habitus meretricis, meretricius, Prov. 7.10. Item, Decor, Honestas, εὐσχημοσύνη, 1. ad Corinth. 12.23. & absque [illegible, ~6 letters] Cum decore, honestate, id est, Honeste, decenter, comiter, εὐσχημόνως, 1. ad Cor. 14.40. ad Rom. 13.13. 1. ad Thess. 4.12. Plur. [illegible, ~6 letters] In uno ex modis, ullo modo, 2. ad Thessal. 2.3.
אִסְלָא Ch. Vectis, palanga, pertica. Plur. אִסְלִין. Respondet Hebraeo מוט.
אסף [illegible, ~6 letters] Syr. Spongia, σπόγγος, Matth. 27. 48. Marc.

page.notes: The Hebrew, Syriac and Greek vocalisation is only approximately reproduced; several Syriac words and some Greek forms are too faint to read with certainty and are marked illegible or with [?]. The Greek word after "καταλάω" is doubtful.
